summary: Send message bodies up to 256 KiB: past 8 KiB the whole text is a file on the sending machine and the claim keeps a preview

replay.detail: No projection or replay change. Existing messages read exactly as before: a message without a text/plain attachments entry has no body_ref and its content is the whole text.

schema.detail: No claim field, table or index is added. The body is an attachments entry with the media type text/plain, and its file lives under <state_dir>/message-bodies on the sending member, outside the database.

rules.detail: Checkpoint rules and admission rules are unchanged.

compatibility.detail: Older builds accept the claim and read the message as its preview, because they keep only image attachments entries. Client API: optional body_ref and body_bytes on message resources and timeline message bodies, limits.max_message_bytes, GET /v1/client/message-bodies/{id}, and the error codes message-too-large, message-store-full and long-message-signature-unsupported. A paired device that signs the whole text of a message over 8 KiB is refused until it signs the preview, hash and size; shorter messages are unchanged. Older clients keep reading the preview. A backup that carries message bodies declares archive version 2, which a build without bodies refuses; a backup of a member with no long bodies is unchanged.

downtime.detail: No restart ordering is required. A long message is read in full by members on this build; others show its preview.

manual.detail: Long message bodies expire from the owner's machine after 30 days by default (ST3_MESSAGE_BODIES_RETENTION_DAYS; 0 keeps them). After that only the preview remains and a reader is told the body expired; the claim and its signature stay valid. The owner's store is limited to 256 MiB per sender and 1 GiB per machine (ST3_MESSAGE_BODIES_ACTOR_MAX_MB, ST3_MESSAGE_BODIES_MAX_MB). Backups made by this build include the long bodies the member owns.

recovery.detail: Rolling back leaves long messages in the log with their previews; the files and expiry markers stay on the owner and are ignored by older builds. A body that expired cannot be recovered except from a backup taken before it.
